title: Renuka @ Rinku & Seema @ Devendra Gavit v. State of Maharashtra
crime_type: Serial Child Kidnapping / Theft Human Shield / Child Homicide
court_or_authority: Supreme Court of India / High Court of Bombay / Sessions Court Kolhapur
source: Supreme Court of India Official Judgment & Indian Kanoon (doc/1628174)
ipc_sections: Section 364 IPC (Kidnapping in order to murder)
Section 201 IPC (Causing disappearance of evidence of offence)
Section 379 IPC (Theft in crowded public places)
location: Kolhapur, Pune, Thane & Nashik, Maharashtra, India
evidence: Recovery of multiple infant remains buried in farm plots and riverbanks across Western Maharashtra based on approver disclosures
Testimony of Kiran Shinde (accused turned approver) detailing the kidnapping and killing timeline of 13 children
Positive test identification of the sisters by surviving parents of abducted toddlers from bus stands and temple fairs
Police arrest memos seizing child clothes and feeding bottles from the traveling gang's vehicle
Medical autopsy reports confirming fatal skull fractures, blunt trauma against pavement stones, and strangulation
modus_operandi: Toured crowded pilgrimage temples, busy bazaars, and state transport bus stands across Western Maharashtra. Snatched infants and toddlers while their parents were distracted. Used the abducted children as 'cover' or 'shields' while pickpocketing crowds (police would not suspect women carrying infants). Whenever a kidnapped child became unruly, cried excessively, or posed risk of detection, the women smashed the infant's head against stones or iron poles, strangled them, and discarded remains in gunny sacks by highways.
personality_disorder: Clinical evaluation noted extreme callousness, total lack of maternal empathy, predatory utilitarian exploitation of vulnerable children, and generational criminal grooming by their mother Anjanabai.
common_traits: Kidnapping infants and toddlers from temple congregations and markets
Using stolen children as human camouflage during pickpocketing
Eliminating children once they became inconvenient or cried
Extreme physical brutality against defenseless toddlers
Operated as a closed matriarchal family crime syndicate
summary: First case in Indian legal history where two female serial offenders were awarded the death penalty, upheld by the Supreme Court of India. Convicted of abducting 13 children and murdering multiple infants between 1990 and 1996, creating foundational jurisprudence on circumstantial approver testimony and aggravated depravity.
